jobs.description:
Company Description
Augusta Richmond County Judicial Center is a public sector organization providing judicial and administrative services to the residents of Augusta, Georgia and the surrounding area. Located at 735 James Brown Boulevard, the Center supports local courts and related justice system operations. Team members contribute to fair, efficient, and accessible legal processes for the community. As a government entity, the Center offers opportunities for public service, professional growth, and engagement with diverse stakeholders. The work environment emphasizes integrity, accountability, and adherence to legal and regulatory standards.

The Case Manager is responsible for oversight and ensuring participants are linked to relevant and effective services; all service efforts are monitored, connected, and in synchrony; and pertinent information gathered during assessment and monitoring is provided to the Adult Felony Accountability Court Coordinator in real time. Case management forms the framework around which the drug court process can credibly and effectively operate.

Key Responsibilities and Performance Standards

Identify and recommend appropriate resources to facilitate access to services for accountability court participants;
Ensure that participants are being properly screened for drug/alcohol abuse, mental health needs, and veteran status as determined appropriate by the staffing team and ensure that the drug lab staff is operating the drug lab in a proper and efficient manner;
Complete weekly case notes, draft agreements, track participant fees and payments, and complete weekly reports while maintaining necessary recordkeeping in accordance with grant requirements;
Work in close cooperation with Judges and the Coordinator to plan and prepare for case staffings, court sessions, graduations, terminations, and grant reporting;
Assess program and participant need, evaluate new resources and establish new contacts while providing services as a Case Manager to participants.
Provide day-to-day supervision of the Case Managers and act as Coordinator in his/her absence.

REQUIRED MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS:

Education: Bachelor's degree from an accredited college or university in social work, psychology, criminal justice, behavior management, public health, sociology, corrections or a related field. Advanced degree and/or licensure or credentials in social work, addiction management or counseling preferred.

Experience: Two (2) years of fieldwork or case management experience to include project or program case management, in the field of addictions, human/family services, health services, public safety, law enforcement or corrections.

Knowledge/Skills/Abilities:

Knowledge of case management practices in the context of a court-supervised substance abuse and mental health program including, but not limited to, state and national best practices
Excellent organizational skills and customer service are of the highest priority as well as competence and temperament to communicate with the legal community, in-house court personnel, Accountability Court participants, and the general public in a fast-paced environment.
Ability to work a full-time standard Court work schedule (Monday through Friday) with flexibility to accommodate evening hours at least once weekly.
Ability to communicate effectively, orally and in writing and make decisions based on experience, good judgment, and established policies and procedure
Ability to exercise a high degree of judgment, tact, diplomacy, discretion, and competence while maintaining an effective and confidential working relationship when dealing with judges, attorneys, courts personnel, service providers, and accountability court participants.
Ability to develop partnerships and foster a spirit of teamwork among participants; develop and supervise, community service and volunteer projects for participants and committees; and to bring people from different agencies together to accomplish the goals of the program.
Skilled in maintaining accurate records and in data processing and case management systems.
Ability to provide proper supervision and training to assigned staff and contractors.
Ability to apply statutory requirements and to understand and comply with state and federal confidentiality laws concerning medical, substance abuse and mental health treatment.
Ability to handle multiple tasks and maintain a professional demeanor when dealing with court personnel and the public at all tim
Ability to set priorities and simultaneously process multiple duties and responsibilitie
Ability to properly supervise staff
Certification(s): This position will not act in a clinical capacity and supervision hours will not be offered if applicant requires clinical licensing hours. Licenses and Certificates in the fields of social work, substance abuse counseling and/or similar fields are not a requirement for employment but are preferred.

Other:

Works closely with the clinical treatment provider(s) and community supervision officers to provide ongoing assessment and communication of the participant's progress and to coordinate referrals to appropriate ancillary service providers

jobs.description:
*Job Summary and Responsibilities*

As our* Imaging Services Program Manager*, you will lead professional operational planning, oversight, development, and collaboration on projects that advance Diagnostic Imaging's strategic objectives, working closely with Diagnostic Imaging leadership, executive leaders, and Diagnostic Imaging Directors to guide analytics and metrics, asset utilization, capital purchasing and procurement support, patient experience and throughput, project management, process improvement and implementation, multi-disciplinary coordination, vendor interfacing, and stakeholder networking.

Every day you will partner with Diagnostic Imaging Administration and business leaders to lead rapid response teams addressing business-critical imaging issues, provide program leadership, thought partnership, analysis, and strategic decision-making support to ensure sustainable, scalable, user-centric solutions are implemented, and drive consistent communication and change management across VMFH Diagnostic Imaging in partnership with other strategic leaders, service lines, and national imaging initiatives to achieve operational efficiencies.

To be successful in your role, you will need to conceptualize and apply sound analytical methods to spearhead program development and monitoring, navigate complex organizational impacts and unique challenges within the Diagnostic Imaging environment, and bring strong initiative, independent judgment, and strategic execution experience while leading teams through the full project lifecycle from discovery through implementation and business value delivery.

In partnership with VMFH Diagnostic Imaging (DI) leadership and executive leaders, works closely with executives to guide the development of strategic and operating plans, metric plans and dashboards, business cases/plans, and support for other strategic planning endeavors within Diagnostic Imaging. Coordinates, initiates and/or facilitates process improvement initiatives/projects for (and/or across) the assigned market(s) within Diagnostic Imaging, including Rapid Process Improvement Workouts; applies knowledge of VMPS and Lean-Six Sigma methodologies to process improvement activities. Provides program leadership, thought partnership, analysis, and strategic decision-making support to initiative sponsors and teams to ensure sustainable and scalable user-centric solutions are developed and implemented to successfully realize business outcomes and drive change within the Diagnostic Imaging environment.
Performs complex data analytics/modeling/forecasting activities in support of operational, business and financial planning and development for Diagnostic Imaging; prepares recurring and special aggregated data reports and related decision support tools by obtaining/manipulating electronic and abstracted data from automated systems and utilizing complex report-writing applications. Oversees, develops and collaborates on projects and planning efforts that advance the strategic objectives of VMFH Diagnostic Imaging (DI); provides support to the VMFH Diagnostic Imaging (DI) executive and management team as requested.
Develops dashboards, scorecards, charts, graphs, tables, diagrams, presentations and reports from various data sources to display, measure and/or summarize clinical outcomes, patient satisfaction, cost/utilization data and other key performance indicators specific to Diagnostic Imaging; may develop analyses relating to demographics, demand, competition, utilization trends, performance improvement, throughput opportunities and growth opportunities specific to assigned market within Diagnostic Imaging. Coordinates the flow of internal communications through a variety of mechanisms (including publications, meetings, website, email, etc.) to advance VMFH Diagnostic Imaging (DI) strategies and support related internal initiatives and change management within the department.
Performs other duties as required.

Bachelors Other and 4-6 years, upon hire or
Equivalent combination of experience., upon hire
None, upon hire

Building upon a legacy of compassionate care and innovation, our organization has evolved over the years through strategic partnerships and integrations to expand our reach and services across the Puget Sound area.

Today, as Virginia Mason Franciscan Health, we remain deeply committed to healing the whole person – body, mind, and spirit – in the communities we serve. This commitment is strengthened by the diverse expertise and shared values brought together through our growth.

Our dedicated providers offer a full spectrum of health care services, from routine wellness to complex disease management, all grounded in rigorous research and education. jobs.title: Clinical Research Assistant / Medical Assistant
jobs.description:
Alcanza is a growing multi-site, multi-phase clinical research company with a network of locations in AL, AZ, FL, GA, IL, MA, MI, MO, NV, VA, SC, TN, TX and Puerto Rico. We have established a strong presence across Phase I-IV studies and several therapeutic areas including vaccine, neurology, dermatology, psychiatry, and general medicine. Join us as we continue to grow.

The Research Assistant (RA)
provides support to the Clinical Research Coordinators (CRCs), Site Manager, Principal and Sub Investigators, and other site staff in compliance with GCP, ICH, HIPAA, FDA Regulations and SOPs. The RA performs clinical, lab, and administrative tasks as needed for the successful operation of the clinical research site.

Essential Job Duties:
In collaboration with other members of the clinical research site team, assists with the execution of assigned studies, and support functions as needed. Responsibilities may include but are not limited to:

Under the direction of the Site Manager/Director and the Principal/Sub Investigators, assists the CRCs and other site staff in their responsibilities by conducting the following according to study protocol:
Assists with the basic screening of patients for study enrollment;
Assists with patient follow-up visits;
Documents in source clinic charts;
Enters data in EDC and answers queries;
Obtains vital signs and ECGs;
May perform blood draws;
Perform basic lab procedures per protocol, such as: blood specimen collection, centrifuge operation, storing and shipping of lab specimens, accountability of specimens and notification of courier for specimen pick-up;
Request and track medical record requests;
Enters data in EDC and answers queries;
Assists the CRC with updating and maintaining logs and filing in charts, and with chart filing; and
Schedules subjects for study visits, conducts appointment reminders, and reschedules visits if needed;

Ensures study related reports and patient results are reviewed by the Research Coordinator and/or investigator in a timely manner.
Assists the CRC and/or Manager with study recruitment, patient enrollment, and tracking as needed;
Maintains strict confidentiality of patients, employees, customers and company information at all times and adheres to HIPAA Guidelines; and
Perform all other duties as requested or assigned.

Minimum Qualifications
: A High School diploma and 1 year of administrative / clinical experience is required. 1 year or more years of clinical research or clinical experience is preferred. Phlebotomy experience required. Bi-lingual (English / Spanish) proficiency is a plus.

Required Skills

Proficiency with computer applications such as Microsoft applications, email, electronic health records, web applications, and the ability to type proficiently (40+ wpm).
Must possess strong organizational skills and attention to detail.
Well-developed written and verbal communication skills.
Well-developed interpersonal and listening skills and the ability to work well independently as well as with co-workers, subjects, managers and external customers.
Ability to effectively handle multiple tasks and adapt to changes in workloads and priorities.
Must be professional, respectful of others, self-motivated, and have a strong work ethic.
Must possess a high degree of integrity and dependability.
Ability to work under minimal supervision, identify problems and implement solutions.
Ability to handle highly sensitive information in a confidential and professional manner, and in compliance with HIPAA guidelines.
Full-time employees regularly scheduled to work at least 30 hours per week are benefits-eligible, with coverage starting on the first day of the month following date of hire.
Medical, dental, vision, life insurance, short and long-term disability insurance, health savings accounts, supplemental insurances, and a 401k plan with a safe harbor match are offered.

Alcanza Clinical Research (“Alcanza”) is a national, collaborative network of clinical research sites, founded on the mission to accelerate the development of new therapies by reducing barriers to clinical research participation for all.

We conduct research on dozens of conditions in several therapeutic areas including psychiatry, neurology, dermatology, and infectious disease. Our work is important to the patients who participate, the scientists who develop these new therapies, and the entire medical community. Because all approved medications require clinical trials, the impact of your work is exponential, reaching many thousands of future patients and improving their quality of life.

Alcanza is a culturally competent organization. We treat each other with dignity, creating an environment where all individuals feel welcome, heard, and respected for their unique perspectives and aspirations. Company Description
Option Care Home Health of California Inc is a home health organization based in Delaware, United States, serving patients who require clinical care in the comfort of their homes. The company focuses on delivering coordinated, high-quality services that support patient recovery, independence, and ongoing wellness. Team members collaborate with healthcare professionals to ensure that care plans are evidence-based and patient-centered. The organization values integrity, accountability, and continuous improvement to better support patients and families. Option Care Home Health offers opportunities for professionals to contribute to research and operational excellence in a supportive environment.
Role Description
The Research Assistant role is a full-time, remote position responsible for supporting clinical and operational research initiatives. Day-to-day tasks include conducting literature reviews, collecting and organizing data, assisting with study design, and supporting the preparation of reports, presentations, and manuscripts. The Research Assistant will collaborate with clinical staff and project leads to ensure data accuracy, maintain documentation, and uphold research protocols and confidentiality standards. Additional responsibilities may include performing basic data analysis, updating research databases, and helping with regulatory or compliance-related documentation. The role requires consistent communication with remote team members and the ability to manage multiple tasks and deadlines independently.
Qualifications

Candidates should possess strong Research and Analytical Skills to support study design, data collection, and interpretation.
Candidates should possess effective Communication skills, including clear written and verbal communication for reports and collaboration with cross-functional teams.
Candidates should possess Laboratory Skills where applicable, such as handling samples, following protocols, and maintaining accurate records.
Candidates should possess Data Analysis skills, including familiarity with basic statistical methods and tools (e.g., Excel, SPSS, or similar software).
Relevant qualifications include a bachelor’s degree in a health-related, scientific, or social science field, or equivalent experience in research support.
Additional beneficial skills include attention to detail, time management, proficiency with office and collaboration software, and familiarity with healthcare or home health environments.
Ability to work independently in a remote setting while maintaining confidentiality and adhering to ethical research standards.
